sermon.title: The Fifth Group, Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing his present truth series, Pastor David G. Kincer reviews the marks of the last days and adds citizens as the fifth necessary but risky group, showing from Jotham, Pilate and Felix that corrupt citizens can bring judgment and manipulate government. He traces God correcting corrupt people from the flood to Sodom, Canaan and the golden calf, and answers critics that God is a King, Judge and Father doing His job.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: his Jotham reference is captioned “2 Chronicles 21 verse 1”; the account of King Jotham is 2 Chronicles 27:1-2 (shown). He gives “2 Kings 15:34” for the Lord sending Rezin and Pekah against Judah, which is 2 Kings 15:37 (shown). The captions read “Acts 16” for Israel becoming a nation and for no one knowing the times; it is rendered “Acts 1:6” (Acts 1:6-7 shown). His figures (20th-century deaths and refugees from a 20th-century atlas, over 2 million people at Sinai) and his statements about homosexuals, humanists, liberals and other groups influencing the government and Supreme Court are his own and are not verified here. Several words are marked [unclear].

chunks.section_question: What are the five ways God brings correction? (Ezekiel 14:21)

scriptures.text_nkjv: For thus says the Lord GOD: “How much more it shall be when I send My four severe judgments on Jerusalem—the sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence—to cut off man and beast from it?

faqs.question: Does God promise blessing when you are mistreated for doing wrong?
faqs.answer: He says if you’re doing good and mistreated, God promised that; but if you’re not doing good, “the Bible says there’s no profit in that when you’re mistreated.”

faqs.question: When does he say the falling away happened?
faqs.answer: He says there had to be a falling away first, and that happened in the dark ages.

faqs.question: Has the gospel been preached to all nations with signs and wonders yet?
faqs.answer: He says we have seen it on regional scales but “we have not seen that on a global scale.”

faqs.question: Why are citizens one of the necessary groups?
faqs.answer: He says if a government doesn’t have citizens to rule over, judge and enforce laws for, it is not necessary, so citizens are the fifth necessary but risky group.

faqs.question: Is government always to blame?
faqs.answer: He says “government isn’t always wrong the people can be wrong.”

faqs.question: Why could Pilate find no fault in Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says Pilate could find no fault with Jesus, signifying that He was the perfect sacrifice lamb for the sins of the world.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has He done?” But they cried out all the more, “Crucify Him!”

faqs.question: What does a loving father do, according to Proverbs 13:24?
faqs.answer: He says “you don’t discipline your kids you hate your kid,” and he who loves his children will discipline and correct them promptly.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who spares his rod hates his son, But he who loves him disciplines him promptly.

faqs.question: How many people does he say civil government killed in the 20th century?
faqs.answer: He cites a 20th century atlas saying civil government killed 262 million people, which he calls democide, murder by government.

faqs.question: Why don’t the nations turn to God after disasters?
faqs.answer: He says even after refugee camps, plagues, famine and war, the nations don’t get it; they think it is normal activity and keep doing worse and worse, like the Bible said.
